hypotheses.statement: For a selector-resolved external function declared nonpayable, both solc/anvil and solang/pallet-contracts reject a nonzero msg.value at the call boundary before executing the body, leaving storage unchanged and emitting no function event.

evidence.note: pay(0) reverted and kept count=0; pay(1) incremented count and emitted Paid; np() with value=1 reverted without changing count; np() with value=0 incremented count. No status/storage/event/revert-reason divergence was reported.

hypotheses.next_probe: Add a receive()/fallback() to the same probe and call the nonpayable function with value to check whether value is rejected by the targeted nonpayable function or rerouted to fallback/receive differently across chains.

hypotheses.statement: A payable function using require(msg.value > 0) behaves equivalently on both chains for the zero/nonzero boundary: value=0 reverts with the expected reason and no state/event effect, while the minimum nonzero value=1 executes the body.

evidence.note: The zero-value require path and the value=1 success path matched across solc and solang; revert_reasons and events were enabled in the oracle and produced no divergence.

hypotheses.next_probe: Change pay() to branch on exact msg.value, e.g. require(msg.value == 1), and test values 0, 1, and 2 to verify equality-vs-inequality value predicates also match.

hypotheses.statement: Native-token unit differences (EVM wei vs pallet-contracts planck/existential-deposit model) did not surface as a behavioral divergence for status-only oracles when comparing payable gating, nonpayable rejection, storage count, and event emission.

evidence.note: All value-transfer semantics probed here agreed despite the known different balance models; balances were not compared, consistent with the seed area guidance.

hypotheses.next_probe: Probe larger value magnitudes near the funding limit, especially a value accepted by anvil but potentially dust/ED-affecting on pallet-contracts, while keeping the oracle to status/storage/events and never comparing balances.
